control_gap: No SMB-specific protocol hardening or access restrictions in place; monitoring alone (SS6.1-MON-1) does not enforce SMB encryption or message signing.
narrative: Network flow to host-000 (Windows 10 server, Low criticality) classified as Benign with 98% ML confidence and no paired CVE. Likelihood=Low (no exploitation pathway) and Impact=Low (non-critical asset) yields Risk=Very Low. Complement SS6.1-MON-1 monitoring with SS6.4-AC-1 (Network Access Control Policy) to enforce SMB security controls (signing, encryption) and reduce residual risk to Very Low.

control_gap: Flow-classification baselines absent; whitelisting rules for benign protocols (SMB) not implemented. Existing monitoring (SS6.1-MON-1) provides visibility but lacks automated benign-flow categorization to reduce false-positive alert noise.
narrative: Network flow to host-005 (Windows 10 firewall, Medium criticality) classified as Benign with 97% ML confidence; zero paired CVE and no KEV listing. Short-duration SMB protocol communication (0.4s, 7 fwd / 5 bwd packets) poses no infiltration, exfiltration, or C2 risk. Likelihood=Low (no exploitable surface, benign traffic commodity); Impact=Low (firewall handling routine protocol, monitoring asset, no consequence). Implement A.13.1.3 (network segregation and access-control baselines) to establish SMB flow signatures and whitelisting rules, reducing false-positive noise and sharpening detection signal-to-noise for actual anomalies.

control_gap: ML classifier confidence at 70% leaves 30% uncertainty; consider detection engine tuning (SS6.3) for future confidence improvement, but not required at Very Low risk.
narrative: host-006 (workstation, Low criticality) exhibits Benign traffic on HTTPS with no paired CVE or active exploitation indicators. ML classifier confidence of 70% is within acceptable tolerance for a low-criticality asset; monitoring control SS6.1-MON-1 provides sufficient visibility. Residual risk remains Low due to workstation asset type, encrypted protocol, and benign network behaviour.

control_gap: Port-based egress filtering and behavioral C2/lateral-movement pattern detection; existing SS6.1-MON-1 monitoring lacks automated anomaly analysis for non-standard port exfiltration.
narrative: ML-classified Benign traffic on Medium-criticality IoT asset host-015 presents suspicious flow behavior (non-standard port 54717, 1.37 ms contact), but 100% classifier confidence and absence of paired CVE support Low likelihood (no threat exploitation vector) and Low impact (no asset criticality × attack consequence product). Existing SS6.1-MON-1 monitoring is insufficient for preventing stealthy lateral movement via non-standard ports. Recommend SS6.2-AC-3 (network access control with port-based egress whitelist) to reduce residual anomaly-detection gaps on IoT segments.

control_gap: No brute-force detection, rate limiting, account lockout, or IDS/IPS rules present. Existing control SS6.7-AC-1 (access control) does not address sustained credential stuffing attacks. Missing: password attempt limits, adaptive rate limiting per IP/session, and real-time brute-force pattern detection.
narrative: Host-054 (Low criticality Linux web server) is under active BruteForce attack targeting CVE-2006-2369, a known-exploited vulnerability (CVSS 7.5, KEV-listed). The sustained HTTP session (57 seconds, 153 requests, 104 responses, 100% ML classifier confidence) demonstrates commodity-class credential stuffing with high likelihood of exploitation; Medium impact reflects server role and compromise consequence. Existing access control (SS6.9-AC-1) does not mitigate brute-force patterns; implement SS6.9-BR-1 (rate limiting, account lockout, and IDS/IPS brute-force rules) to reduce residual risk from High to Low.

control_gap: Absence of patch management; existing network control (SS6.7-NET-2) provides volumetric mitigation only and cannot remediate code-execution risk from unpatched CVE-2017-0144 (EternalBlue). Asset requires urgent vulnerability assessment and critical patch deployment.
narrative: Asset host-003 (Windows Server workstation, Low criticality) is exposed to DDoS traffic on HTTP (2.05 ms flow, minimal packets) while harboring an unpatched critical vulnerability (CVE-2017-0144, CVSS 9.3, KEV-listed for active exploitation in the wild). The simultaneous presence of commodity DDoS probing and a code-execution vulnerability suggests potential multi-stage attack reconnaissance. Network control SS6.7-NET-2 mitigates volumetric DDoS availability impact but does not address the persistent lateral-movement and code-execution risk; immediate vulnerability patching is required to reduce LIKELIHOOD from Very High to Low and eliminate the threat-asset pairing.

control_gap: DDoS-specific rate limiting and flood-pattern IDS tuning; existing network segmentation (SS6.7-NET-2) provides partial mitigation but lacks active volumetric-attack defense.
narrative: CVE-2017-7679 (CVSS 7.5, KEV-listed) is actively exploited against high-criticality workstation host-007 via DDoS traffic with 100% ML classifier confidence. Likelihood assessed as High: CVSS 7.5 (high range), KEV status confirms active exploitation, and DDoS is a commodity attack with high base-rate exploitability. Impact is Medium: asset is high-criticality but the attack vector is volumetric/availability (not data exfiltration or control compromise), and the asset is a workstation rather than a critical infrastructure server. Existing network controls partially mitigate; DDoS-specific rate limiting and IDS pattern refinement are required to reduce residual risk.
